user_persona_scenario: First-time investor in Month 2 with -₹45 loss on ₹1,000 Nifty SIP. Anxious because family says 'stock market drowns your money'. Asking: 'Should I stop or let it run?'
human_evaluator_feedback: Missed explaining to user that is okay to have dips in returns during SIP investment journey, but good for explaining the user in hinglish in his terms.
mvp_response_before_human_feedback: Flat SEBI refusal + neutral buttons only: 'Main aapko yeh nahi bata sakta ki kya khareedein, bechein ya stop karein... Kisi SEBI adviser se salah lein. 3 options hain: date badalna, ₹100 karna, ya cancel.' (Cold, zero emotional context)
mvp_response_after_human_feedback: Contextual Reassurance + SEBI Compliance: 'Main advice nahi de sakta... Lekin mutual fund concepts ke hisab se, shuruati 2 mahino mein -₹45 jaisa chhota dip aana bilkul normal hai. Market roz fluctuate hoti hai, NAV thodi girne par return temporary negative dikh sakta hai, lekin aapki units safely aapke account mein rehti hain. Long-term SIP mein short-term utar-chadav aana aam baat hai.' + 3 neutral options.
product_deck_takeaway: Reassurance via unit mechanics, not false promises. Prevents panic stops without violating SEBI advisor rules.

user_persona_scenario: User invested ₹10,000/mo across 4 Small Cap funds due to Instagram influencer hype. Small caps are now correcting, influencers stopped talking, and user feels like an idiot trapped by hype.
human_evaluator_feedback: Missed explaining that its okay to have some short term less returns during the SIP journey. And there is higher risk in small cap returns
mvp_response_before_human_feedback: Standard generic disclaimer: 'I can't tell you what to buy, sell or stop. I can explain how things work... For advice, a SEBI-registered adviser can help. 3 neutral options: move date, reduce to ₹100, cancel.' (Zero recognition of Small Cap risk)
mvp_response_after_human_feedback: Risk Category Education + SEBI Compliance: 'I can't tell you what to buy, sell or stop... From a mutual fund concept standpoint, Small Cap funds invest in smaller companies that carry higher volatility and risk, meaning they tend to experience sharper corrections during market downturns. In early periods of an SIP, short-term negative swings or lower returns are a normal part of market cycles, while your instalments accumulate units at different NAVs.' + 3 neutral options.
product_deck_takeaway: Empowers regretful users by contextualizing high-beta small cap risk rather than dismissing their frustration.

user_persona_scenario: User's friend made 40% in Tata Motors stock in 4 months; user's large-cap SIP made 4.2%. User feels like wasting youth on slow mutual funds and asks if they should quit SIP for direct stocks.
human_evaluator_feedback: Remained Neutral for not advising any stock or fund but didnt explained the compunding works in long term and its okay to have low returns in short term
mvp_response_before_human_feedback: Neutral refusal with 3 actions: 'I can't tell you what to buy, sell or stop... For advice, a SEBI RIA can help. Neutral options: move date, reduce to ₹100, cancel.' (Compliant, but didn't address the stock vs SIP comparison)
mvp_response_after_human_feedback: Asset Class Grounding + SEBI Compliance: 'I can't tell you what to buy, sell or stop... Conceptually, individual direct stocks and diversified mutual fund SIPs operate differently: individual stocks can experience rapid short-term moves in either direction, whereas an equity SIP is designed for steady rupee-cost averaged compounding over the long term. In early periods, returns can be modest and short-term lower returns are a normal part of the investing journey.' + 3 neutral options.
product_deck_takeaway: Curbing equity FOMO through foundational compounding mechanics without passing judgment or giving advice.
